summary: This subsystem defines how GraphQL schemas are represented in Grackle and how they are built from SDL text. A `Schema` is an immutable collection of `NamedType` declarations (`ScalarType`, `EnumType`, `InterfaceType`, `ObjectType`, `UnionType`, `InputObjectType`) plus directive definitions and extensions, with nullability and lists modelled by the `NullableType`/`ListType` wrappers and by-name references modelled by `TypeRef`. Schemas are normally constructed via the compile-time-validated `schema"..."` string interpolator (or the runtime `Schema(text): Result[Schema]` factory), which parse SDL into an `Ast.Document` (`GraphQLParser`), build the typed model (`SchemaParser`), and run an extensive battery of structural checks (`SchemaValidator`). The model is the ground truth used by mappings and elaborators: types are compared with `=:=`/`<:<` and referenced by name through `schema.ref(...)` so that `TypeRef`s support mutual recursion and value-equality. The subsystem also covers custom scalars, schema directives (definition, validation, the built-ins `@skip`/`@include`/`@deprecated`/`@specifiedBy`/`@oneOf`), type extensions (`extend ...`), and rendering a `Schema` back to SDL via `SchemaRenderer` (used by `Schema.toString`).

keyConcepts.name: schema"..." string interpolator
keyConcepts.explanation: The idiomatic way to define a schema. Defined in version-specific syntax files (scala-2/syntax2.scala via Scala 2 macros, scala-3/syntax3.scala via the typelevel `Literally` macro) and surfaced through `import grackle.syntax._`. It parses and fully validates the SDL at COMPILE time; an invalid schema is a compile error (message prefixed with `Invalid schema:` and 🐞 bullets). It expands to `Schema(s, CompiletimeParsers.schemaParser).toOption.get`, so it yields a bare `Schema`, not a `Result[Schema]`.

keyConcepts.name: Schema(text): Result[Schema]
keyConcepts.explanation: The runtime factory in `object Schema`. Unlike the interpolator it returns a `Result[Schema]` (success or accumulated validation `Problem`s), so it is what you use when the SDL is not known at compile time or when you want to inspect validation errors. `Schema.apply` takes an implicit `SourcePos`.

keyConcepts.name: Type vs NamedType
keyConcepts.explanation: `Type` is the root sealed trait for every GraphQL type. `NamedType` is the subset with a schema-defined `name` (`ScalarType`, `EnumType`, `InterfaceType`, `ObjectType`, `UnionType`, `InputObjectType`, plus `TypeRef`). `ListType` and `NullableType` are unnamed type *modifiers* that wrap another `Type`.

keyConcepts.name: Nullability is inverted vs SDL
keyConcepts.explanation: In Grackle's model, types are non-null by DEFAULT (a bare `ScalarType`/`TypeRef` is already non-null). Optionality is represented by explicitly wrapping in `NullableType`. This is the OPPOSITE of GraphQL SDL where `String` is nullable and `String!` is non-null. The parser (`SchemaParser.mkType`) therefore wraps every non-`!` type in `NullableType`. Use `.nullable`, `.nonNull`, `.isNullable` to manipulate.

keyConcepts.name: Lists via ListType
keyConcepts.explanation: A GraphQL `[T]` becomes `NullableType(ListType(NullableType(T)))` for the fully-nullable case (list nullable, elements nullable). `[T!]!` becomes `ListType(T)`. `.list`, `.item`, `.isList` operate on this. The parser limits list nesting depth to `maxListTypeDepth` (default 5).

keyConcepts.name: TypeRef and by-name references
keyConcepts.explanation: `TypeRef(schema, name)` is a lazy, by-name reference to a type defined in a schema. It is how mutually recursive types are expressed and, crucially, the ONLY type representation that can be meaningfully compared with `==`. Obtain a checked ref with `schema.ref(name)` (throws `IllegalArgumentException` if undefined) or an unchecked one with `schema.uncheckedRef(name)`. `.dealias` resolves a `TypeRef` to its target; `.exists` reports whether the target is defined.

keyConcepts.name: =:= / <:< / dealias
keyConcepts.explanation: `a =:= b` is type equivalence that sees through aliases/TypeRefs (preferred over `==`). `a <:< b` is the subtype relation (object<:<implemented interface, member<:<union, list/nullable covariance). `.dealias` strips TypeRef aliasing. `.nominal_=:=` compares by underlying name.

keyConcepts.name: Custom scalars
keyConcepts.explanation: Declared in SDL with `scalar Name` (optionally `@specifiedBy(url: ...)`). They produce a `ScalarType` with `isBuiltIn == false`. The schema layer only records the scalar's name; how its values are encoded/decoded is supplied elsewhere via `LeafMapping[A]` plus `Value` extractors in the mapping/elaborator. `Value.checkValue`/`checkVarValue` pass primitives and enum values through unchanged for non-built-in scalars.

keyConcepts.name: Schema directives & DirectiveDef
keyConcepts.explanation: Custom directives are declared in SDL with `directive @name(args) [repeatable] on LOC1 | LOC2` producing a `DirectiveDef`. Applied occurrences are `Directive(name, args)`. The five built-ins (`@skip`, `@include`, `@deprecated`, `@specifiedBy`, `@oneOf`) are always appended (`DirectiveDef.builtIns`). `Directive.validateDirectivesForSchema` checks every applied directive against its definition's locations, repeatability and argument types. `@deprecated`/`@specifiedBy`/`@oneOf` have first-class accessors (`isDeprecated`, `specifiedByURL`, `isOneOf`).

keyConcepts.name: Schema validation (SchemaValidator)
keyConcepts.explanation: On construction the parser runs `SchemaValidator.validateSchema`, accumulating `Problem`s for: references to undefined types, duplicate type/field/enum-value definitions, non-object or duplicate union members, interface implementation conformance (missing fields, wrong field subtype, mismatched args), transitive-interface obligations, interface cycles, type-extension target mismatches, and directive validity. All failures surface as `Result.Failure(NonEmptyChain[Problem])`.

keyConcepts.name: Root operation types & schemaType
keyConcepts.explanation: If no explicit `schema { query mutation subscription }` block is present, Grackle synthesises a default schema type referencing types named `Query`, `Mutation`, `Subscription` (only those that exist). `schema.queryType` is non-optional and will throw `NoSuchElementException` if there is no query root. `mutationType`/`subscriptionType` are `Option`.

keyConcepts.name: Type extensions
keyConcepts.explanation: `extend type/interface/union/enum/input/scalar/schema ...` parse into `TypeExtension`/`SchemaExtension` values stored separately on the schema; `schema.types` and `schema.schemaType` lazily merge extensions onto base types. Validated by `validateTypeExtensions` (e.g. cannot apply an Object extension to a non-object, cannot extend a non-existent type).

keyConcepts.name: Ast layer
keyConcepts.explanation: `grackle.Ast` is the untyped parse tree (`Document = List[Definition]`, `TypeDefinition`, `FieldDefinition`, `Ast.Type.{Named,List,NonNull}`, `Ast.Value`, `DirectiveLocation`, etc.). `GraphQLParser.parseText` produces an `Ast.Document`; `SchemaParser.parseDocument` lowers it into the typed `Schema` model. The `doc"..."` interpolator yields a raw `Ast.Document`.

keyTypes.signature: sealed trait NamedType extends Type { def name: String; override def dealias: NamedType = this; def description: Option[String]; def directives: List[Directive] }

minimalExamples.title: Define a schema with the compile-time-validated interpolator
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle.Schema
import grackle.syntax._

val schema: Schema =
  schema"""
    type Query {
      hero(episode: Episode!): Character!
      character(id: ID!): Character
    }
    enum Episode {
      NEWHOPE
      EMPIRE
      JEDI
    }
    interface Character {
      id: String!
      name: String
      friends: [Character!]
      appearsIn: [Episode!]
    }
    type Human implements Character {
      id: String!
      name: String
      friends: [Character!]
      appearsIn: [Episode!]
      homePlanet: String
    }
  """

val QueryType     = schema.ref("Query")
val CharacterType = schema.ref("Character")
minimalExamples.explanation: Canonical pattern (verbatim from the StarWars demo). The schema text is parsed and fully validated AT COMPILE TIME; an invalid schema fails compilation. `schema.ref(name)` returns a TypeRef for use in mappings/elaborators and is safe to compare with ==. Requires `import grackle.syntax._`.

minimalExamples.explanation: When SDL is not statically known, use `Schema(text): Result[Schema]`. Validation errors are accumulated as Problems (here the typo 'Episod' is flagged). Adapted directly from SchemaSuite 'undefined types' tests.

minimalExamples.title: Custom scalars and an enum in a schema
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle.syntax._

val schema =
  schema"""
    type Query {
      movieById(id: UUID!): Movie
      moviesByGenre(genre: Genre!): [Movie!]!
    }
    scalar UUID
    scalar Date
    enum Genre {
      DRAMA
      ACTION
      COMEDY
    }
    type Movie {
      id: UUID!
      title: String!
      genre: Genre!
      releaseDate: Date!
    }
  """

val UUIDType = schema.ref("UUID")   // a ScalarType, isBuiltIn == false

Omitting the required url argument fails validation with 'Value of type String required for url in directive specifiedBy'.

minimalExamples.title: Define and apply a custom schema directive
minimalExamples.explanation: Directives are declared with `directive @name(args) on LOCATIONS` and applied with `@name(...)`. Applied directives become `Directive(name, args)` on the relevant Field/type and are validated against their DirectiveDef (location, repeatability, arg types). Adapted from SchemaDirectivesSuite.

minimalExamples.title: Inspect nullability, lists and references on a type
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle.syntax._

val schema =
  schema"""
    type Query { posts: [Post] }
    type Post  { id: Int!  title: String }
  """

val PostType = schema.ref("Post")

PostType.field("id").get.isNullable      // false  (Int!)
PostType.field("title").get.isNullable   // true   (String)
schema.ref("Query").field("posts").get.isList  // true (after stripping outer nullable)
PostType =:= schema.ref("Post")          // true (alias-aware equivalence)
minimalExamples.explanation: Demonstrates that in Grackle's model bare types are non-null and optional ones are wrapped in NullableType (opposite of SDL surface syntax). `=:=` is the alias-aware equivalence to prefer over ==. Derived from SchemaSuite / SDLSuite parse examples.

minimalExamples.title: Round-trip SDL via Schema.toString
minimalExamples.explanation: SchemaParser parses SDL to a Schema; Schema.toString (SchemaRenderer.renderSchema) renders it back to SDL. Built-in directive definitions are omitted from the rendering. Verbatim shape from SDLSuite 'deserialize schema' tests.

gotchas: Nullability is INVERTED relative to SDL. In Grackle's in-memory model types are non-null by default and optionality is an explicit NullableType wrapper. So SDL `String` parses to `NullableType(StringType)` and `String!` parses to `StringType`. Anyone reading the model expecting `!`-style semantics will get it backwards.

The `schema"..."` interpolator returns a bare `Schema`, NOT a `Result[Schema]` - it expands to `Schema(s, ...).toOption.get`. Validation happens at compile time, so a bad schema is a COMPILE error. Use the runtime `Schema(text): Result[Schema]` when you need to handle/inspect validation Problems at runtime.

`schema.queryType` is non-optional and calls `.get`; if the schema has no query root type it throws `NoSuchElementException` (SchemaSuite: `intercept[NoSuchElementException](schema"scalar Foo".queryType)`). `mutationType`/`subscriptionType` are safe Options.

Compare types with `=:=` (alias-aware) not `==`. Plain `==` distinguishes a type from a `TypeRef` alias to it, which is almost never what you want. Exception: `TypeRef`s obtained from the SAME schema via `schema.ref` ARE designed to be `==`-comparable - that is their whole purpose for use in elaborator pattern matches.

`schema.ref(name)` throws IllegalArgumentException if the name is not defined in the schema; `schema.uncheckedRef(name)` does NOT check (it can produce a dangling TypeRef whose `.exists` is false and whose navigation methods return None/false - see SchemaSuite 'operations on undefined types').
`TypeRef`'s case-class constructor is `private[grackle]`; you cannot `new TypeRef(...)` from user code. Always go through `schema.ref` / `schema.uncheckedRef`.

Every parsed schema silently gets the five built-in directive definitions appended (DirectiveDef.builtIns: skip, include, deprecated, specifiedBy, oneOf). SchemaRenderer deliberately omits these from `toString`, so a round-tripped schema will not show them even though `schema.directives` contains them.

Object/interface/union/enum/input types must be non-empty: an object/interface with zero fields, a union with zero members, an enum with zero values, or an input object with zero fields is a parse failure (e.g. 'object type X must define at least one field').

Custom scalar names are case-sensitive and references are validated: a typo like using `Long` without declaring `scalar Long`, or `CCid` vs declared `CCId`, produces 'Reference to undefined type ...'. The five built-in scalar names (Int/Float/String/Boolean/ID) are always available without declaration; re-declaring them via `scalar Int` etc. is accepted and maps to the built-in.

`@oneOf` input objects may not have any non-nullable fields - declaring one fails at parse time with 'oneOf input object type X may not have non-nullable field(s): ...'. At value-checking time, exactly one member must be supplied and it must be non-null (Value.checkValue enforces this).

A type that implements an interface must ALSO directly declare every interface that interface transitively implements, otherwise you get 'Type X does not directly implement transitively implemented interface Y'. Interface implementation also checks field presence, that the implementing field type is a `<:<` subtype, and that argument lists match exactly (by name and type, via `==` not `<:<`).
Interface implements-cycles are rejected ('Interface cycle starting from ...'); union members must be object types ('Non-object type ... included in union ...').

The schema/custom-scalar model only records the scalar's NAME. It does not know how to serialise/parse the scalar - that lives in the mapping layer (LeafMapping[A] + Value extractor objects). Defining `scalar UUID` alone does nothing at runtime until a LeafMapping and the relevant Value pattern-matching are provided (see ScalarsSuite MovieMapping).

GraphQLParser.defaultConfig imposes limits: maxSelectionDepth=100, maxSelectionWidth=1000, maxInputValueDepth=5, maxListTypeDepth=5. Deeply nested list type modifiers in SDL (beyond 5) or very large queries will be rejected by the parser unless you supply a custom Config.

summary: A `Mapping[F]` is the central abstraction that ties a GraphQL `Schema` to an underlying data source. It holds three things: the `schema`, a `TypeMappings` catalog (a `Seq[TypeMapping]` indexed for lookup), and a `selectElaborator`. From these it builds a `QueryCompiler` and `QueryInterpreter`, and exposes top-level entry points `compileAndRun`/`compileAndRunSubscription`. The catalog distinguishes `TypeMapping`s (`ObjectMapping` for object/interface/union types; `LeafMapping[T]` for scalar/enum types) from `FieldMapping`s nested inside object mappings (`CursorField`, `ValueField`, `Delegate`, `EffectField`, `RootEffect`, `RootStream`, plus circe's `CirceField`/`CursorFieldJson`). Each `TypeMapping` is selected by a `MappingPredicate` (`TypeMatch`, `PathMatch`, `PrefixedTypeMatch`) so mappings can be context/path sensitive, and the whole catalog is validated against an unfolding of the schema before the compiler is built. Concrete subtypes — `ValueMapping` (in-memory Scala values), `ComposedMapping` (federating other mappings via `Delegate`/`combineAndRun`), `CirceMapping`, `GenericMapping`, `SqlMapping` — override `mkCursorForMappedField` to produce backend-specific `Cursor`s.

keyConcepts.name: Mapping[F]
keyConcepts.explanation: The abstract base (modules/core/src/main/scala/mapping.scala). A subclass supplies `implicit val M: MonadThrow[F]`, `val schema: Schema`, and `val typeMappings: TypeMappings` (and usually overrides `selectElaborator`). It derives `compiler`, `interpreter`, `componentElaborator`, `effectElaborator`, and offers `compileAndRun`/`compileAndRunSubscription`/`combineAndRun`. Everything else (TypeMapping/FieldMapping/Cursor catalog, validation failures) is nested inside this trait, so members like `ObjectMapping`, `CursorField`, `RootEffect`, `LeafCursor` are path-dependent on a `Mapping` instance.

keyConcepts.name: TypeMappings catalog
keyConcepts.explanation: `final class TypeMappings` wraps a `Seq[TypeMapping]` plus mutable indices (typeIndex, predicatedTypeIndex, typeFieldIndex, predicatedTypeFieldIndex). It is the lookup engine: `typeMapping(context)`, `objectMapping(context)`, `fieldMapping(context|cursor, fieldName)`, `encoderForLeaf`. Built via `TypeMappings(...)` (checked) or `TypeMappings.unchecked(...)`. Built-in leaf mappings for String/Int/Float/Boolean/ID are always appended automatically. A `List[TypeMapping]` is converted to `TypeMappings` by the implicit `TypeMappings.fromList`, which is why test/demo code can write `val typeMappings = List(...)`.

keyConcepts.name: TypeMapping vs FieldMapping
keyConcepts.explanation: `TypeMapping` (sealed) maps a whole GraphQL type and carries a `MappingPredicate` (its `tpe` comes from the predicate). The two concrete kinds are `ObjectMapping` (object/interface/union — holds `fieldMappings`) and `LeafMapping[T]` (scalar/enum — holds an `Encoder[T]`). `FieldMapping` (trait) maps a single field within an `ObjectMapping` and exposes `fieldName`, `hidden`, `subtree`, `pos`. The mapping-to-data wiring happens in `mkCursorForMappedField`, which pattern-matches on the `FieldMapping` subtype to build the right child `Cursor`.

keyConcepts.name: MappingPredicate
keyConcepts.explanation: Decides when a `TypeMapping` applies, returning an `Option[Int]` priority (highest wins; ties are an `AmbiguousTypeMappings` error). `TypeMatch(tpe)` matches the type anywhere (priority 0). `PathMatch(path)` matches a type reached via a specific field path (preferred for context-sensitivity). `PrefixedTypeMatch(prefix, tpe)` is the legacy `PrefixedMapping` semantics. `ObjectMapping(tpe)(...)`, `ObjectMapping(path)(...)`, `LeafMapping[T](tpe)` etc. are convenience constructors that build the predicate for you.

keyConcepts.name: Cursor production (mkCursorForMappedField)
keyConcepts.explanation: The core override point. `Mapping.mkCursorForMappedField` (protected) handles `EffectMapping` and `CursorField`; backend traits override it: `ValueMappingLike` handles `ValueField` by applying `f: T => Any` to the parent focus; `CirceMappingLike` handles `CirceField`/`CursorFieldJson`; `ComposedMapping` returns a `ComposedCursor`. `mkCursorForField` (final) resolves the `FieldMapping` from the catalog then delegates here.

keyConcepts.name: Effect & root fields
keyConcepts.explanation: `EffectMapping` (subtree=true) covers fields that perform F-effects. `EffectField(name, handler, required, hidden)` defers an effect via an `EffectHandler[F]`. `RootEffect` runs an initial F-effect for a root query/mutation field, producing a `(Query, Cursor)`; `RootStream` is the streaming analogue used for subscriptions. Both have `apply`, `computeCursor`, `computeChild`, and (RootEffect only) `computeUnit` constructors; CirceMapping adds `computeJson`/`computeEncodable` via implicit syntax. `mapping.rootEffect`/`mapping.rootStream` look them up.

keyConcepts.name: selectElaborator / compilerPhases
keyConcepts.explanation: `val selectElaborator: SelectElaborator = SelectElaborator.identity` is the per-mapping query-rewriting phase (typically overridden to translate field arguments into `Filter`/`Unique`/`Eql` predicates and to stash args in the `Env` via `Elab.env`). `compilerPhases = List(selectElaborator, componentElaborator, effectElaborator)`; `componentElaborator` is derived from `Delegate` field mappings and `effectElaborator` from `EffectField`s. The `compiler` lazy val validates the catalog (`unsafeValidateIfChecked`) then builds a `QueryCompiler`.

keyConcepts.name: combineAndRun (federation)
keyConcepts.explanation: `combineAndRun(queries: List[(Query, Cursor)]): F[Result[List[ProtoJson]]]` is called by the interpreter (queryinterpreter.scala:784) at the end of a stage to evaluate deferred sub-queries grouped by the mapping responsible for them. The default runs each query one-shot and combines the ProtoJson results; mappings that can batch (e.g. SQL) override it to issue a single combined query. This is the mechanism behind `Delegate`/`ComposedMapping` cross-backend joins.

keyConcepts.name: Mapping validation
keyConcepts.explanation: `validate(severity)` unfolds the schema from the root operation types and reports `ValidationFailure`s: `MissingTypeMapping`, `AmbiguousTypeMappings`, `MissingFieldMapping`, `DeclaredFieldMappingIsHidden`, `ObjectTypeExpected`, `LeafTypeExpected`, `ReferencedTypeDoesNotExist`, `UnusedTypeMapping`, `UnusedFieldMapping`. `unsafeValidate`/`validateInto` raise. A checked `TypeMappings` is validated automatically the first time `compiler` is forced.

keyTypes.name: Mapping
keyTypes.signature: abstract class Mapping[F[_]] { implicit val M: MonadThrow[F]; val schema: Schema; val typeMappings: TypeMappings }
keyTypes.purpose: Root abstraction tying a Schema to a data source; supplies query entry points and the TypeMapping/FieldMapping/Cursor catalog as nested members.

keyTypes.signature: def defaultRootCursor(query: Query, tpe: Type, parentCursor: Option[Cursor]): F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]]

keyTypes.name: mkCursorForMappedField
keyTypes.signature: protected def mkCursorForMappedField(parent: Cursor, fieldContext: Context, fm: FieldMapping): Result[Cursor]
keyTypes.purpose: Primary override point: build the child Cursor for a resolved FieldMapping. Base handles EffectMapping and CursorField; backends extend it.

keyTypes.name: TypeMappings
keyTypes.signature: final class TypeMappings private (val mappings: Seq[TypeMapping], ...) { def typeMapping(context: Context): Option[TypeMapping]; def objectMapping(context: Context): Option[ObjectMapping]; def fieldMapping(context: Context, fieldName: String): Option[FieldMapping]; def fieldMapping(parent: Cursor, fieldName: String): Result[Option[(Cursor, FieldMapping)]]; def validate(severity: Severity = Severity.Warning): List[ValidationFailure] }
keyTypes.purpose: Indexed catalog of TypeMappings with lookup and validation. Constructed via the companion's apply/unchecked.

keyTypes.name: TypeMappings companion
keyTypes.signature: object TypeMappings { def apply(mappings: Seq[TypeMapping]): TypeMappings; def apply(mappings: TypeMapping*)(implicit dummy: DummyImplicit): TypeMappings; def unchecked(mappings: Seq[TypeMapping]): TypeMappings; def unchecked(mappings: TypeMapping*)(implicit dummy: DummyImplicit): TypeMappings; implicit def fromList(mappings: List[TypeMappingCompat]): TypeMappings; val empty: TypeMappings }

keyTypes.name: TypeMapping
keyTypes.signature: sealed trait TypeMapping extends TypeMappingCompat with Product with Serializable { def predicate: MappingPredicate; def pos: SourcePos; def tpe: NamedType = predicate.tpe; def showMappingType: String = productPrefix }
keyTypes.purpose: Base of all type-level mappings; its GraphQL type comes from its predicate.

keyTypes.name: MappingPredicate
keyTypes.signature: trait MappingPredicate { def tpe: NamedType; def apply(ctx: Context): Option[Int]; def continuationContext(ctx: Context): Option[Context] }
keyTypes.purpose: Determines applicability + priority of a TypeMapping in a Context. Implementations: TypeMatch, PrefixedTypeMatch, PathMatch.

keyTypes.name: MappingPredicate.TypeMatch
keyTypes.signature: case class TypeMatch(tpe: NamedType) extends MappingPredicate
keyTypes.purpose: Matches a type in any context (priority 0).

keyTypes.name: MappingPredicate.PathMatch
keyTypes.signature: case class PathMatch(path: Path) extends MappingPredicate
keyTypes.purpose: Matches a type reached via a specific field path; preferred for context-sensitive mappings.

keyTypes.name: MappingPredicate.PrefixedTypeMatch
keyTypes.signature: case class PrefixedTypeMatch(prefix: List[String], tpe: NamedType) extends MappingPredicate
keyTypes.purpose: Legacy PrefixedMapping semantics: matches a type with a given path prefix.

keyTypes.name: ObjectMapping
keyTypes.signature: abstract class ObjectMapping extends TypeMapping { def fieldMappings: Seq[FieldMapping]; def fieldMapping(fieldName: String): Option[FieldMapping] }
keyTypes.purpose: Maps an object/interface/union type to its field mappings.

keyTypes.name: ObjectMapping companion
keyTypes.signature: object ObjectMapping { case class DefaultObjectMapping(predicate: MappingPredicate, fieldMappings: Seq[FieldMapping])(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends ObjectMapping; def apply(predicate: MappingPredicate)(fieldMappings: FieldMapping*)(implicit pos: SourcePos): ObjectMapping; def apply(tpe: NamedType)(fieldMappings: FieldMapping*)(implicit pos: SourcePos): ObjectMapping; def apply(path: Path)(fieldMappings: FieldMapping*)(implicit pos: SourcePos): ObjectMapping; def apply(tpe: NamedType, fieldMappings: List[FieldMapping])(implicit pos: SourcePos): ObjectMapping }

keyTypes.name: FieldMapping
keyTypes.signature: trait FieldMapping extends Product with Serializable { def fieldName: String; def hidden: Boolean; def subtree: Boolean; def pos: SourcePos; def showMappingType: String = productPrefix }
keyTypes.purpose: Base of all field-level mappings inside an ObjectMapping.

keyTypes.name: LeafMapping
keyTypes.signature: trait LeafMapping[T] extends TypeMapping { def encoder: Encoder[T]; def scalaTypeName: String; def pos: SourcePos }
keyTypes.purpose: Maps a scalar or enum GraphQL type to a circe Encoder. (There is NO PrimitiveMapping type — LeafMapping is the leaf/primitive construct.)

keyTypes.name: LeafMapping companion
keyTypes.signature: object LeafMapping { case class DefaultLeafMapping[T](predicate: MappingPredicate, encoder: Encoder[T], scalaTypeName: String)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends LeafMapping[T]; def apply[T: TypeName](predicate: MappingPredicate)(implicit encoder: Encoder[T], pos: SourcePos): LeafMapping[T]; def apply[T: TypeName](tpe: NamedType)(implicit encoder: Encoder[T], pos: SourcePos): LeafMapping[T]; def apply[T: TypeName](path: Path)(implicit encoder: Encoder[T], pos: SourcePos): LeafMapping[T]; def unapply[T](lm: LeafMapping[T]): Option[(Type, Encoder[T])] }

keyTypes.name: CursorField
keyTypes.signature: case class CursorField[T](fieldName: String, f: Cursor => Result[T], encoder: Encoder[T], required: List[String], hidden: Boolean)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends FieldMapping { def subtree = false }
keyTypes.purpose: Computes a leaf field value from the parent Cursor; `required` lists sibling fields/attributes the function depends on.

keyTypes.name: CursorField companion
keyTypes.signature: object CursorField { def apply[T](fieldName: String, f: Cursor => Result[T], required: List[String] = Nil, hidden: Boolean = false)(implicit encoder: Encoder[T], di: DummyImplicit): CursorField[T] }

keyTypes.signature: case class Delegate(fieldName: String, mapping: Mapping[F], join: (Query, Cursor) => Result[Query] = ComponentElaborator.TrivialJoin)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends FieldMapping { def hidden = false; def subtree = true }

keyTypes.name: EffectField
keyTypes.signature: case class EffectField(fieldName: String, handler: EffectHandler[F], required: List[String] = Nil, hidden: Boolean = false)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends EffectMapping
keyTypes.purpose: A field whose value is produced by a deferred batched effect handler.

keyTypes.name: selectElaborator
keyTypes.signature: val selectElaborator: SelectElaborator = SelectElaborator.identity
keyTypes.purpose: Per-mapping query elaboration phase; override to translate field arguments into query algebra (Filter/Unique/Eql) and env bindings.

keyTypes.name: ValueMapping / ValueMappingLike

keyTypes.name: ValueObjectMapping
keyTypes.signature: object ValueObjectMapping { case class DefaultValueObjectMapping(predicate: MappingPredicate, fieldMappings: Seq[FieldMapping], classTag: ClassTag[_])(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends ObjectMapping; class Builder(predicate, pos){ def on[T](fieldMappings: ValueFieldMapping[T]*)(implicit classTag: ClassTag[T]): ObjectMapping }; def apply(predicate: MappingPredicate)(implicit pos: SourcePos): Builder; def apply(tpe: NamedType)(implicit pos: SourcePos): Builder; def apply(path: Path)(implicit pos: SourcePos): Builder; def apply[T](tpe: NamedType, fieldMappings: List[ValueFieldMapping[T]])(implicit classTag: ClassTag[T], pos: SourcePos): ObjectMapping }

keyTypes.purpose: Cursor over an arbitrary Scala value; narrowsTo uses the ValueObjectMapping ClassTag.

keyTypes.signature: abstract class ComposedMapping[F[_]](implicit val M: MonadThrow[F]) extends Mapping[F] { case class ComposedCursor(context: Context, env: Env) extends AbstractCursor }
keyTypes.purpose: Federating mapping: overrides mkCursorForMappedField to yield a ComposedCursor; fields are wired to sub-mappings via Delegate.

keyTypes.signature: case class CursorFieldJson(fieldName: String, f: Cursor => Result[Json], required: List[String], hidden: Boolean = false)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends CirceFieldMapping

keyTypes.signature: case class CirceField(fieldName: String, value: Json, hidden: Boolean = false)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends CirceFieldMapping
keyTypes.purpose: Maps a field to a constant Json value (circe module).

minimalExamples.title: LeafMapping for custom scalar/enum types
minimalExamples.explanation: From modules/core/src/test/scala/compiler/ScalarsSuite.scala. Each LeafMapping[T](tpe) needs an implicit circe Encoder[T] in scope (e.g. Genre.genreEncoder). LeafMapping is how custom scalars/enums are encoded — there is no separate PrimitiveMapping type. Built-in String/Int/Float/Boolean/ID leaf mappings are added automatically by TypeMappings.

gotchas: No `PrimitiveMapping` exists in the codebase. The leaf/primitive construct is `LeafMapping[T]` (modules/core/src/main/scala/mapping.scala). Built-in leaf mappings for String, Int, Float, Boolean and ID are appended automatically by `TypeMappings.mkMappings`, so you only declare LeafMappings for custom scalars/enums.

`CursorFieldJson` and `CirceField` are NOT in core — they live in the circe module (modules/circe/src/main/scala/circemapping.scala) on `CirceMappingLike`. They are only usable from a CirceMapping/CirceMappingLike subtype.

All catalog members are path-dependent types nested inside `Mapping[F]` (ObjectMapping, ValueField, CursorField, RootEffect, LeafCursor, the ValidationFailure case classes, etc.). You must reference them through a concrete Mapping instance/subclass; e.g. validation matches `case List(M.MissingTypeMapping(_))`.

`typeMappings = List(...)` only compiles because of the implicit `TypeMappings.fromList(List[TypeMappingCompat])`. If you need to skip validation, you must use `TypeMappings.unchecked(...)` explicitly — a plain List is always treated as checked.

A checked `TypeMappings` is validated lazily the first time the `compiler` val is forced (`unsafeValidateIfChecked`), which throws a `ValidationException`. Validation does NOT run at construction time, so a bad mapping can look fine until the first query is compiled.

Ambiguity is an error: if two TypeMappings match a context with equal (highest) predicate priority you get `AmbiguousTypeMappings`. `TypeMatch` has priority 0; `PathMatch`/`PrefixedTypeMatch` have higher priority proportional to path length, so a path-specific mapping wins over a bare type mapping.

Declared schema fields must have a non-hidden field mapping. `MissingFieldMapping` fires for a declared field with no mapping; `DeclaredFieldMappingIsHidden` fires if you mark a declared field's mapping `hidden = true`. Hidden is meant for synthetic/attribute fields used only as `required` dependencies of other fields.

`ValueObjectMapping` narrowing for interfaces/unions relies on a runtime `ClassTag` (`classTag.runtimeClass.isInstance(focus)`), so you MUST supply the correct concrete `[T]` type parameter — e.g. `ValueObjectMapping[Human](...)`. A wrong/erased type param breaks `narrowsTo`/`narrow`.

`compileAndRun` runs `compileAndRunSubscription` and expects exactly one element; a query against a Subscription-shaped root (or any stream producing 0 or >1 results) raises IllegalStateException. Use `compileAndRunSubscription` for subscriptions.

`RootEffect`/`RootStream` are private case classes — construct them only through the companion `apply`/`computeCursor`/`computeChild`/`computeUnit` factories, never with `new`. `computeChild` requires the root query to have an extractable child or it raises an internal error 'Root query has unexpected shape'.

`CursorField.f` and `ValueField.f` should declare every sibling field/attribute they read from the cursor in `required` (CursorField) so the interpreter knows to materialize those dependencies; ValueField operates only on the parent focus value, not on sibling cursors.

Overriding `combineAndRun` is the supported way to batch deferred subqueries (the default runs each query one-shot). SQL mappings override it; if you override it incorrectly the result list must stay aligned with the input query list or results will be mismatched.

`PrefixedMapping(tpe, mappings)` is a backwards-compat shim returning a `TypeMappingCompat.PrefixedMappingCompat`; it throws IllegalArgumentException unless all entries share the same `tpe`. Prefer `PathMatch` predicates for new code (the source comments say PathMatch should be preferred unless PrefixedTypeMatch semantics are strictly required).

summary: The Cursor abstraction (modules/core/src/main/scala/cursor.scala) is Grackle's read-only navigator over an arbitrary backing data model during GraphQL query execution. A Cursor knows its focus (the current value, typed Any), its GraphQL tpe via a Context, and exposes type-driven navigation: field, narrow/narrowsTo (interface/union narrowing), asLeaf (scalar/enum to Json), asList/preunique (lists and the antecedent of Unique), asNullable/isDefined (nullables), plus environment (Env) accessors. The QueryInterpreter (modules/core/src/main/scala/queryinterpreter.scala) walks a Query against a root Cursor, dispatching on (query, tpe.dealias) in runValue/runFields/runList to build a ProtoJson - an opaque, possibly-partial JSON tree that may contain DeferredJson (EffectJson) subtrees delegated to component/effect interpreters. completeAll then batches and resolves those deferred subtrees stage-by-stage and substitutes the results back into the enclosing JSON. Throughout, errors and warnings are accumulated rather than thrown using the four-armed Result type (Success/Warning/Failure/InternalError).

keyConcepts.name: Cursor
keyConcepts.explanation: A position within an abstract data model during query interpretation. Carries a focus (the value, typed Any), a Context (schema path + result/alias path + GraphQL type), an optional parent, and an Env. All navigation methods return Result so failures (wrong type, missing field) are accumulated, not thrown. Concrete cursors (ValueCursor, CirceCursor, generic CursorBuilder cursors, SqlMapping cursors) implement the type-driven navigation against their specific backing model.

keyConcepts.name: Context
keyConcepts.explanation: Immutable record of position in the output tree: rootTpe, path (schema field names, reversed/innermost-first), resultPath (path with query aliases applied), and typePath (the GraphQL Type at each level). tpe is typePath.head (or rootTpe at the root). forField/forFieldOrAttribute/asType derive child contexts. Note equals compares rootTpe with =:= and only path/resultPath (not typePath), and hashCode is just resultPath.hashCode.

keyConcepts.name: focus / tpe duality
keyConcepts.explanation: Every Cursor pairs an untyped runtime value (focus: Any) with the GraphQL Type it is expected to represent (tpe, from context). Navigation methods pattern-match on (tpe, focus) together - e.g. ValueCursor.isList is true only when tpe is a ListType AND focus is a List[_]. Mismatch yields a Result.internalError. cursorCompatible in the interpreter guards each step by stripping nullable/list wrappers and comparing leaf-ness or nominal equality.

keyConcepts.name: Type-directed interpretation
keyConcepts.explanation: runValue dispatches on (query, tpe.dealias): scalar/enum -> asLeaf; object/interface/union -> runFields; ListType -> runList; NullableType -> asNullable then recurse; Unique -> preunique then runList(unique=true); plus Environment, Component, TransformCursor cases. runFields handles Select, Group, Narrow, Count, Effect, __typename Introspect, Environment, TransformCursor and returns (resultName, ProtoJson) pairs.

keyConcepts.name: ProtoJson
keyConcepts.explanation: An opaque type (type ProtoJson <: AnyRef) of a partially-constructed result. A ProtoJson is either a complete io.circe.Json, or one of the package-private DeferredJson/ProtoObject/ProtoArray/ProtoSelect wrappers when some subtree is deferred. Constructors (fromJson, fromFields, fromDisjointFields, fromValues, select, component, effect) collapse to plain Json eagerly when all children are already Json, so deferral wrappers only appear when genuinely needed.

keyConcepts.name: Deferred / staged evaluation
keyConcepts.explanation: Component joins and Effect fields produce EffectJson(mapping, handler, query, cursor) leaves inside the ProtoJson. complete/completeAll gather all DeferredJson leaves, group them by (mapping, handler), run each batch (via mapping.combineAndRun or handler.runEffects), recursively complete the next stage, then scatter results back using an IdentityHashMap keyed on the deferred nodes. This is how composite/batched and effectful resolution works.

keyConcepts.name: Env
keyConcepts.explanation: A sealed key/value environment (EmptyEnv / NonEmptyEnv) threaded through cursors and queries. Cursor.env[T](name) looks up the local env then walks parents; fullEnv accumulates parent-to-child; withEnv adds values. Query.Environment nodes inject env during elaboration/execution (Env.addFromQuery).

keyConcepts.name: Error accumulation via Result
keyConcepts.explanation: Result[+T] has four cases: Success, Warning(problems, value) (a value AND non-fatal problems), Failure(problems) (no value, GraphQL errors), and InternalError(throwable). flatMap/combine carry and merge problems; the interpreter uses Warning to keep partial data while collecting field-level errors, and runOneShot converts a top-level Failure into Warning(errs, Json.Null) so a data:null + errors response is produced.

keyTypes.purpose: The core read-only navigator over a backing data model. Pairs an untyped focus value with the GraphQL Context/Type at that position.

keyTypes.purpose: Cast the focus to a concrete Scala type T, yielding a descriptive error Result if the runtime class does not match.

keyTypes.signature: def preunique: Result[Cursor]
keyTypes.purpose: Yield a Cursor suitable as the antecedent of a Unique operation - re-types the focus as a list (tpe.nonNull.list) so runList(unique=true) can pull out the single element. AbstractCursor's default errors; ValueCursor/CirceCursor override to wrap when focus is actually a list/array.

keyTypes.purpose: Interface/union narrowing. narrowsTo tests run-time membership of subtpe; narrow returns a Cursor re-typed to subtpe (used for Narrow query nodes and __typename resolution).

keyTypes.signature: abstract class AbstractCursor extends Cursor { def isLeaf: Boolean = false; def asLeaf: Result[Json] = ...; def preunique: Result[Cursor] = ...; def isList = false; ... def field(fieldName: String, resultName: Option[String]): Result[Cursor] = Result.internalError(...) }
keyTypes.purpose: Base class giving every navigation method a sensible error default, so a concrete cursor only overrides the cases its model actually supports.

keyTypes.name: Cursor.ProxyCursor
keyTypes.signature: class ProxyCursor(underlying: Cursor) extends Cursor { /* delegates every method to underlying */ }

keyTypes.name: Cursor.ListTransformCursor
keyTypes.signature: case class ListTransformCursor(underlying: Cursor, newSize: Int, newElems: Seq[Cursor]) extends ProxyCursor(underlying)
keyTypes.purpose: List proxy that substitutes an alternative element set/size - the result of a TransformCursor over a list (e.g. filter/order/limit re-projection).

keyTypes.name: Cursor.NullCursor / NullFieldCursor
keyTypes.signature: case class NullCursor(underlying: Cursor) extends ProxyCursor(underlying); case class NullFieldCursor(underlying: Cursor) extends ProxyCursor(underlying)
keyTypes.purpose: NullCursor always reports isDefined=false / asNullable=None (forces null). NullFieldCursor wraps every child field result in a NullCursor.

keyTypes.name: Cursor.DeferredCursor

keyTypes.purpose: A cursor that defers construction of the real cursor until a given path prefix is traversed, invoking mkCursor at the end of the path. Used to splice a sub-model in part-way down a query.

keyTypes.name: Context
keyTypes.signature: case class Context(rootTpe: Type, path: List[String], resultPath: List[String], typePath: List[Type]) { lazy val tpe: Type; def asType(tpe: Type): Context; def forField(fieldName: String, resultName: Option[String]): Result[Context]; def forFieldOrAttribute(...): Context; def parent: Option[Context] }
keyTypes.purpose: Tracks schema path, alias-applied result path, and the GraphQL type stack for a cursor position. Key derivations: asType (re-type current level), forField (descend), parent (ascend).

keyTypes.name: Context companion
keyTypes.signature: object Context { def apply(rootTpe: Type): Context; def apply(rootTpe: Type, fieldName: String, resultName: Option[String]): Option[Context]; def apply(path: Path): Result[Context] }
keyTypes.purpose: Build a root Context for a type, or a context at a field/path. Context(IntType) is the common idiom in tests to root a leaf cursor.

keyTypes.name: Env
keyTypes.signature: sealed trait Env { def add[T](items: (String, T)*): Env; def add(env: Env): Env; def contains(name: String): Boolean; def get[T: ClassTag](name: String): Option[T]; def isEmpty: Boolean; def getR[A: ClassTag: TypeName](name: String): Result[A]; def addFromQuery(query: Query): Env }; object Env { def empty: Env; def apply[T](items: (String, T)*): Env }
keyTypes.purpose: Immutable typed environment carried by cursors and queries. get is type-checked via ClassTag.unapply, so a wrongly-typed lookup returns None.

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter
keyTypes.signature: class QueryInterpreter[F[_]](mapping: Mapping[F]) { def run(query: Query, rootTpe: Type, env: Env): Stream[F, Result[Json]] }
keyTypes.purpose: Top-level driver. run interprets a query and completes all deferred/staged subtrees, yielding a Stream of fully-resolved Result[Json] (a stream because subscriptions yield many).

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter.runRootValue / runOneShot / runSubscription
keyTypes.signature: def runRootValue(query: Query, rootTpe: Type, parentCursor: Cursor): F[Result[ProtoJson]]; def runOneShot(query: Query, rootTpe: Type, rootCursor: Cursor): F[Result[ProtoJson]]; def runSubscription(query: Query, rootTpe: Type, rootCursor: Cursor): Stream[F, Result[ProtoJson]]
keyTypes.purpose: Single-stage entry points producing a possibly-deferred ProtoJson. runOneShot splits queries into pure/introspection/effectful, runs each, and merges; runRootValue builds a default root cursor then runValue.

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter.runValue / runFields / runList
keyTypes.signature: def runValue(query: Query, tpe: Type, cursor: Cursor): Result[ProtoJson]; def runFields(query: Query, tpe: Type, cursor: Cursor): Result[List[(String, ProtoJson)]]; def runList(query: Query, tpe: Type, parent: Cursor, unique: Boolean, nullable: Boolean): Result[ProtoJson]
keyTypes.purpose: The recursive interpretation core. runValue dispatches on (query, tpe.dealias); runFields produces named field results for object/interface/union types; runList iterates list cursors applying filter/order/offset/limit and handles Unique.

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter.cursorCompatible
keyTypes.signature: def cursorCompatible(tpe: Type, cursorTpe: Type): Boolean
keyTypes.purpose: Guard run at each level: strips nullable/list wrappers and accepts if both are leaves or are nominally equal. A mismatch produces an internalError instead of silently mis-walking.

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter.ProtoJson
keyTypes.signature: type ProtoJson <: AnyRef; object ProtoJson { def fromJson(value: Json): ProtoJson; def fromFields(fields: Seq[(String, ProtoJson)]): ProtoJson; def fromDisjointFields(fields: Seq[(String, ProtoJson)]): ProtoJson; def fromValues(elems: Seq[ProtoJson]): ProtoJson; def select(elem: ProtoJson, fieldName: String): ProtoJson; def component[F[_]](mapping: Mapping[F], query: Query, cursor: Cursor): ProtoJson; def effect[F[_]](mapping: Mapping[F], handler: EffectHandler[F], query: Query, cursor: Cursor): ProtoJson; def isDeferred(p: ProtoJson): Boolean; def mergeProtoJson(elems: Seq[ProtoJson]): ProtoJson }
keyTypes.purpose: Opaque partial-result tree. Constructors collapse to plain circe Json when all children are Json, otherwise retain ProtoObject/ProtoArray/ProtoSelect/EffectJson wrappers for later completion.

keyTypes.name: QueryInterpreter.complete / completeAll
keyTypes.signature: def complete[F[_]: Monad](pj: ProtoJson): F[Result[Json]]; def completeAll[F[_]: Monad](pjs: List[ProtoJson]): F[Result[List[Json]]]
keyTypes.purpose: Resolve deferred subtrees: gather DeferredJson leaves, batch by (mapping, handler), run each batch, recursively complete the next stage, then scatter results back into the enclosing JSON via an IdentityHashMap.

keyTypes.name: Query.EffectHandler
keyTypes.signature: trait EffectHandler[F[_]] { def runEffects(queries: List[(Query, Cursor)]): F[Result[List[Cursor]]] }
keyTypes.purpose: Pluggable batch effect resolver. completeAll calls runEffects with all (continuation-query, cursor) pairs deferred to this handler, then re-enters runValue for each returned cursor.

keyTypes.name: Mapping.RootCursor / defaultRootCursor
keyTypes.signature: case class RootCursor(context: Context, parent: Option[Cursor], env: Env) extends AbstractCursor { def focus: Any = (); override def field(fieldName: String, resultName: Option[String]): Result[Cursor] = mkCursorForField(this, fieldName, resultName) }; def defaultRootCursor(query: Query, tpe: Type, parentCursor: Option[Cursor]): F[Result[(Query, Cursor)]]
keyTypes.purpose: The synthetic cursor at the query root (focus is Unit); its field method delegates into the mapping's mkCursorForField to enter the real model.

keyTypes.name: ValueCursor (reference concrete impl)
keyTypes.signature: case class ValueCursor(context: Context, focus: Any, parent: Option[Cursor], env: Env) extends Cursor
keyTypes.purpose: Canonical Cursor over plain Scala values: matches on (tpe, focus) for isList/asList/asNullable/preunique/narrowsTo, and uses mkChild to build child cursors with re-typed context.

keyTypes.name: CirceCursor (reference concrete impl)
keyTypes.signature: case class CirceCursor(context: Context, focus: Json, parent: Option[Cursor], env: Env) extends Cursor
keyTypes.purpose: Cursor over a circe Json document: isLeaf/asLeaf validate the Json shape against the GraphQL scalar/enum type; narrowsTo checks required fields are present.

keyTypes.name: CursorBuilder (generic derivation)
keyTypes.signature: trait CursorBuilder[T] { def tpe: Type; def build(context: Context, focus: T, parent: Option[Cursor] = None, env: Env = Env.empty): Result[Cursor]; final def contramap[A](f: A => T): CursorBuilder[A] }
keyTypes.purpose: Typeclass that produces a Cursor for a Scala value of type T at a given Context. The most direct, test-covered way to construct a Cursor by hand.

minimalExamples.title: Build a leaf cursor and render it as Json
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle._
import grackle.generic.CursorBuilder
import grackle.ScalarType.IntType
import io.circe.Json

val result: Result[Json] =
  for {
    c <- CursorBuilder[Int].build(Context(IntType), 23)
    _  = assert(c.isLeaf)
    l <- c.asLeaf
  } yield l

// result == Result.Success(Json.fromInt(23))
minimalExamples.explanation: CursorBuilder is the simplest way to obtain a real Cursor. Context(IntType) roots it at a scalar type; isLeaf is true and asLeaf yields the circe Json. Verbatim shape from DerivationSuite 'primitive types have leaf cursor builders'.

minimalExamples.title: Descend into a nullable field, then asLeaf
minimalExamples.explanation: field descends by GraphQL field name (None = no alias). Because `name` is nullable in the schema, the child cursor is nullable: asNullable returns Result[Option[Cursor]], and toResultOrError turns an absent value into an error. From DerivationSuite 'product types have cursor builders'.

minimalExamples.title: Traverse a list field
minimalExamples.explanation: asNullable unwraps the nullable wrapper, then asList(List) yields one child Cursor per element. Each element is itself a leaf cursor here. From DerivationSuite 'cursor builders can be resolved for nested types'.

minimalExamples.title: Narrow an interface cursor to a concrete subtype

minimalExamples.explanation: compileAndRun is the high-level entry that elaborates the query and drives QueryInterpreter.run end-to-end (runOneShot -> runValue/runFields -> completeAll). This is how the interpreter is exercised in practice; the Cursor walking happens internally. From DerivationSuite 'simple query'. needsDb=false because the generic StarWars data is in-memory.

minimalExamples.title: Construct a ProtoJson and complete it
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle.QueryInterpreter.ProtoJson
import io.circe.Json
import cats.effect.IO

// A fully-concrete ProtoJson collapses straight to Json
val pj: ProtoJson = ProtoJson.fromFields(Seq(
  "a" -> ProtoJson.fromJson(Json.fromInt(1)),
  "b" -> ProtoJson.fromJson(Json.fromString("x"))
))
assert(!ProtoJson.isDeferred(pj))

val completed: IO[Result[Json]] = QueryInterpreter.complete[IO](pj)
// completed == Result.Success({ "a": 1, "b": "x" })
minimalExamples.explanation: ProtoJson is the interpreter's partial-result type. When every field is already Json, fromFields/fromDisjointFields collapse to a plain Json node, isDeferred is false, and complete returns it unchanged. Deferred subtrees (component/effect) would instead require batched resolution inside completeAll. Derived from the ProtoJson public API in queryinterpreter.scala.

gotchas: Cursor navigation methods return Result, never throw, and have permissive error defaults. AbstractCursor.field/asLeaf/asList/asNullable/preunique all default to Result.internalError, so calling the wrong one for the focus type yields an error Result rather than a compile error or exception - you must match the method to the cursor's actual type (checked via isLeaf/isList/isNullable first).

focus is typed Any and the value/type must agree. ValueCursor.isList is true only when BOTH tpe is a ListType AND focus is a List[_]; a ListType tpe with a non-list focus silently reports isList=false and asList errors. Always keep the backing value in sync with the Context type.

Context.equals and hashCode are deliberately partial: equals ignores typePath (compares rootTpe via =:= plus path and resultPath only) and hashCode is just resultPath.hashCode. Two contexts at the same alias path but different concrete types compare equal - relevant if you key maps on Context.
path/resultPath/typePath are stored innermost-first (reversed). Context.forField prepends, and code that renders a path does context.path.reverse.mkString("/"). Don't assume root-to-leaf ordering.

asNullable returns Result[Option[Cursor]] - two layers. A present nullable is Result.Success(Some(c)); absent is Result.Success(None); a type mismatch is Result.internalError. The interpreter maps None to Json.Null. Forgetting the Option layer (e.g. expecting a Cursor directly) is a common mistake.

preunique does NOT return the unique element - it re-types the focus as a list (tpe.nonNull.list) so the caller (runValue's Unique case) can then runList with unique=true. runList then errors with 'No match' (size 0, non-nullable), 'Multiple matches' (size > 1), or returns null (size 0, nullable).

cursorCompatible is enforced at the start of runValue, runFields, and inside runList's element loop. If a custom Cursor reports a tpe that doesn't strip-match the query type, you get 'Mismatched query and cursor type in runValue/runFields/runList' internal errors rather than a useful message - keep mkChild/asType context re-typing correct.

ProtoJson is an opaque type (type ProtoJson <: AnyRef) whose internal cases (DeferredJson/EffectJson/ProtoObject/ProtoArray/ProtoSelect) are package-private to QueryInterpreter. You can only build it via the ProtoJson.* constructors and inspect via isDeferred - you cannot pattern-match its structure from outside the module.

Constructors collapse eagerly: fromFields/fromDisjointFields/fromValues/select return plain Json the moment all children are Json. So isDeferred is frequently false even for objects/arrays; deferral only appears when a component/effect leaf is present. Tests that assert on deferral must include a real deferred subtree.

fromDisjointFields assumes field names are disjoint and does NOT merge duplicates (it just wraps), whereas fromFields calls mergeFields first. runFields uses fromDisjointFields for the object case but pre-merges via mergeFields in the Group-with-type-case path - mixing them up can produce duplicate keys.

completeAll substitutes deferred results using a java.util.IdentityHashMap keyed on the DeferredJson nodes - results are matched by object identity, not equality. Re-creating or copying an EffectJson node after it has been gathered would break the substitution.

runOneShot turns a top-level Result.Failure into Result.Warning(errs, ProtoJson.fromJson(Json.Null)) so the response is data:null + errors. This means a hard failure at the root still yields a Success/Warning-shaped Json result downstream - check for Warning problems, not just Failure, when inspecting errors.

RootStream is only valid in subscriptions: runOneShot returns an internalError 'RootStream only permitted in subscriptions' if a root-stream field appears in a non-subscription query, and runSubscription rejects more than one root selection ('Only one root selection permitted for subscriptions').

DeferredCursor.field errors unless the requested fieldName equals deferredPath.head; it walks the fixed path one step at a time and only invokes mkCursor at the final step. It cannot be used to navigate arbitrary fields - only the pre-declared path.

Env.get is type-checked at runtime via classTag[T].unapply, so a key present but stored as the wrong type returns None (not an error). Use envR/getR to get a descriptive Result error instead of a silent None.

summary: The Query algebra is a sealed `Query` ADT that represents a GraphQL operation as a tree of interpretable nodes (Select, Group, Unique, Filter, Limit, Offset, OrderBy, Count, Component, Effect, Environment, Narrow, TransformCursor, Empty, plus pre-elaboration `UntypedSelect`/`UntypedFragmentSpread`/`UntypedInlineFragment` precursors). A `QueryCompiler` turns a GraphQL query string into an executable `Operation` by parsing it (via `QueryParser`) into untyped algebra, validating variables/fragments/field-mergeability, then folding a sequence of `Phase`s over the tree. Each phase runs inside the `Elab` monad (`StateT[Result, ElabState, T]`), which threads the schema, the current `Context`, query variables, fragments, a local elaboration `Env`, accumulated attributes, and a pending child-transform through the traversal. The pivotal phase is `SelectElaborator`: a mapping supplies a `PartialFunction[(TypeRef, String, List[Binding]), Elab[Unit]]` that consumes field arguments and rewrites each `UntypedSelect` into a directly-interpretable `Select` wrapping `Filter`/`Unique`/`Limit`/`OrderBy`/`Count`/etc. Built-in phases (IntrospectionElaborator, VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator, MergeFields, ComponentElaborator, EffectElaborator, QuerySizeValidator) handle introspection, variable substitution + skip/include + fragment expansion, field merging, multi-mapping composition, effects, and size limits.

keyConcepts.name: Query ADT vs Untyped precursors
keyConcepts.explanation: `Query` is a sealed trait. After parsing, the tree consists of `UntypedSelect`/`UntypedFragmentSpread`/`UntypedInlineFragment` nodes (carrying raw `Binding` args and `Directive`s). Compiler phases progressively rewrite these into the interpretable algebra: `Select`, `Group`, `Unique`, `Filter`, `Limit`, `Offset`, `OrderBy`, `Count`, `Narrow`, `Component`, `Effect`, `Environment`, `TransformCursor`, and the terminal `Empty`. A node like `Filter`/`Unique`/`Limit` is what the interpreter actually evaluates; `UntypedSelect` is not directly interpretable.

keyConcepts.name: Two-stage Select: UntypedSelect -> Select
keyConcepts.explanation: Parsing produces `UntypedSelect(name, alias, args, directives, child)`. `VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator` substitutes variables into the `Binding` values and drops skip/include-guarded subtrees but keeps it untyped. `SelectElaborator` then types/normalises the args against the schema field, eliminates them by running the mapping's `Elab[Unit]`, and emits `Select(name, alias, child')` — optionally wrapped in `Environment(env, ...)` when the elaborator bound env vars, and merged with extra attribute selects.

keyConcepts.name: Elab monad
keyConcepts.explanation: `type Elab[T] = StateT[Result, ElabState, T]`. It threads `ElabState` (schema, current `Context`, vars, fragments, current query, localEnv, attributes, pending childTransform, and a parent for push/pop) through the traversal and accumulates GraphQL errors/warnings via `Result`. The `Elab` object exposes combinators: `Elab.context`, `Elab.schema`, `Elab.vars`, `Elab.transformChild`, `Elab.env(...)`, `Elab.addAttribute`, `Elab.failure`, `Elab.warning`, `Elab.push`/`Elab.pop`, `Elab.hasField`/`hasSibling`. Elaborators almost never touch `ElabState` directly — they compose these combinators.

keyConcepts.name: transformChild: argument elimination
keyConcepts.explanation: A `SelectElaborator` case returns `Elab.transformChild(child => ...)`. The returned function is captured in `ElabState.childTransform` and applied to the *already-elaborated* child in `SelectElaborator.transform`. This is how field arguments are turned into algebra: `Elab.transformChild(child => Unique(Filter(Eql(CharacterType / "id", Const(id)), child)))` rewrites `character(id:...) { ... }` into a `Unique`/`Filter` over the selection set. Multiple `transformChild` calls compose via `andThen`.

keyConcepts.name: Phase pipeline order
keyConcepts.explanation: `compileOperation` always prepends `IntrospectionElaborator(level)` (unless Disabled), then `VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator :: MergeFields :: phases`, where `phases` is the mapping's `compilerPhases` (default `List(selectElaborator, componentElaborator, effectElaborator)`). Each phase runs `phase.transformFragments *> phase.transform(acc)` folded left over the query. Order matters: variables/fragments are resolved and fields merged *before* the user's SelectElaborator sees a clean typed tree.

keyConcepts.name: Env and Environment
keyConcepts.explanation: `Env` (in cursor.scala) is an immutable string-keyed, type-tagged bag (`EmptyEnv`/`NonEmptyEnv`). During elaboration `Elab.env("x" -> v)` writes to the node's *local* env (`ElabState.localEnv`); if non-empty after elaborating a Select, it is materialised as an `Environment(env, select)` node so the value reaches the interpreter, where a `CursorField` reads it via `cursor.env[Int]("x")`. The whole compile can also be seeded with an external `env` (e.g. `Env("secure" -> true)`) passed to `compile`/`compileAndRun`.

keyConcepts.name: Context push/pop
keyConcepts.explanation: Elaboration walks into child selections by `Elab.push(childCtx, child)` (saving the parent state) and `Elab.pop` afterwards. `Context.forField(fieldName, alias)` computes the child's type context. `hasSibling` is implemented by inspecting the parent state's query. This is the mechanism that lets an elaborator know its position in the schema (`TypeRef`) and inspect neighbouring selections.

keyConcepts.name: addAttribute (synthetic selects)
keyConcepts.explanation: `Elab.addAttribute(name, query)` records a synthetic field that is merged into the elaborated Select via `mergeQueries(e1 :: attrs.map { case (nme, child) => Select(nme, child) })`. Used to inject computed/hidden fields (e.g. a `Count` to compute `hasMore` for pagination) that the client never asked for but a `CursorField` needs.

gotchas: Leaf vs non-leaf subselection is validated, not silently allowed: a leaf field with a non-empty `{ ... }` fails with "Leaf field 'x' of T must have an empty subselection set"; a non-leaf field with an empty selection fails with "Non-leaf field 'x' of T must have a non-empty subselection set". See `validateSubselection` and CompilerSuite invalid-subselection tests.

Unknown arguments fail compilation: `elaborateFieldArgs` rejects any arg name not declared on the schema field ("Unknown argument(s) 'quux' in field character of type Query"). A SelectElaborator case can only match args that survived this check.

Argument matching in SelectElaborator is positional/structural on the *normalised* arg list. `elaborateFieldArgs` permutes args into schema-declared order and fills defaults, so cases like `List(Binding("offset", IntValue(o)), Binding("limit", IntValue(l)))` assume that canonical order, not source order. If your pattern doesn't match, the field is left with its args un-eliminated.

Optional/absent arguments arrive as `AbsentValue`, not `NullValue`. Elaborators must match `Binding("namePattern", AbsentValue)` separately from a provided value (see WorldMapping `numCities`). Forgetting the AbsentValue case means the elaborator silently no-ops.

`Elab.transformChild` callbacks compose with `andThen`, not replace: `ElabState.addChildTransform` chains each transform via `childTransform.andThen(_.flatMap(f))`. Two cases that both call transformChild on the same node both run, in order.

`Elab.env(...)` writes only to the *local* env of the current node; it becomes an `Environment` node wrapping that Select. It is NOT visible to siblings, only to the node's own children/cursor. `hasSibling`/sibling inspection goes through the parent state, a different mechanism.

Compiler auto-prepends phases: regardless of your `compilerPhases`, the pipeline is `IntrospectionElaborator? :: VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator :: MergeFields :: yourPhases`. So your SelectElaborator always sees variable-substituted, fragment-expanded, field-merged, typed `Select` nodes — never raw fragment spreads or variable refs.

`SelectElaborator.transform` only fires on `UntypedSelect`; ComponentElaborator/EffectElaborator fire on already-typed `Select`. Ordering in `compilerPhases` matters: selectElaborator must run before componentElaborator/effectElaborator (the default order), or the latter see UntypedSelect and fall through to `super.transform`.

`mergeQueries` (typed) and `mergeUntypedQueries` (untyped) are distinct: MergeFields uses the untyped merger; mixing them on the wrong stage silently drops or fails to merge selects. They key on `(name, alias)` and recursively merge children; `__typename` and adjacent `Narrow`s of the same type get special handling.

Variable validation runs before phases and reports BOTH undefined and (when `reportUnused=true`, the default) unused variables and fragments as warnings/errors. Set `reportUnused=false` to suppress unused-warnings (e.g. for persisted/partial queries).

Query shorthand (`{ ... }`, no `query` keyword) parses to `UntypedQuery(None, ...)`. The compiler refuses to combine a nameless shorthand op with other operations ("Query shorthand cannot be combined with multiple operations") and requires `name=` to disambiguate when multiple named ops are present.

`Env.get[T]` is type-tag filtered via `classTag[T].unapply`: a value stored as the wrong runtime type returns `None`, not the value. `Elab.envE`/`Env.getR` turn that miss into a descriptive Result failure; plain `env[T]` silently yields None.

`Count` replaces the child it is built from rather than wrapping the original selection: `Elab.transformChild(_ => Count(Select("friends")))` discards the incoming child entirely. The original scalar field's empty child is intentionally thrown away.

`QuerySizeValidator` counts a `Count(_)` node and any empty-child Select as depth+1/width+1, and resolves fragment spreads via the fragment map. It must be added as a user phase (e.g. `super.compilerPhases :+ querySizeValidator`); it is not on by default.

summary: Grackle models query-time filtering, ordering, and paging as a small reified algebra layered on the `Query` ADT. A `Term[T]` is a serializable, introspectable function `Cursor => Result[T]` (so interpreters like the SQL module can compile it into a WHERE/ORDER BY clause instead of running it in-memory); `Path` builds typed term paths from a schema `Type` (e.g. `CountryType / "population"`). `Predicate extends Term[Boolean]` and its case classes (`Eql`, `NEql`, `Lt`/`LtEql`/`Gt`/`GtEql`, `And`/`Or`/`Not`, `In`, `Contains`, `IsNull`, `Matches`, `StartsWith`, plus the SQL-module `Like`) are the leaves of `Filter(pred, child)`. Ordering and paging are separate `Query` nodes: `OrderBy(OrderSelections(...), child)`, `Offset(n, child)`, `Limit(n, child)`, and `Count(child)`. Developers wire user arguments to these nodes inside a `SelectElaborator` using the `Elab` API (chiefly `Elab.transformChild`), and the `FilterOrderByOffsetLimit` constructor/extractor assembles the four-node stack in the canonical order. Paging beyond plain offset/limit (counted totals, "has more", nested paging) is implemented by combining these nodes with `Count`, `CursorField`, `TransformCursor`, and the elaboration environment — there is no built-in Relay/connection (edges/pageInfo/endCursor) type in this codebase.

keyConcepts.name: Term[T] as a reified function
keyConcepts.explanation: `Term[T] extends Product with Serializable` and is essentially a reified `Cursor => Result[T]` (`def apply(c: Cursor): Result[T]`). It is deliberately NOT an arbitrary function so interpreters can introspect it (via `children`, `fold`, `exists`, `forall`, `forallR`) and compile it to a backend query (e.g. SQL WHERE clauses). This is the foundational abstraction for filtering and ordering.

keyConcepts.name: Path / asTerm (UniquePath vs ListPath)
keyConcepts.explanation: `Path` is a typed cursor path rooted at a `Type`. You build one with `Type./(field)` (e.g. `CountryType / "population"`), and an implicit (`Term.path2Term` / `TermLow.path2ListTerm`) converts it to a `Term[A]`. `Path.asTerm` chooses `PathTerm.UniquePath` for scalar paths and `PathTerm.ListPath` for list-valued paths based on `rootTpe.pathIsList(path)`. This is why `Contains` takes a `Term[List[T]]` for a list field while `Eql` takes a `Term[T]` for a scalar.

keyConcepts.name: Predicate ADT
keyConcepts.explanation: `Predicate extends Term[Boolean]`. Leaves include equality (`Eql`/`NEql` need `Eq[T]`), ordering (`Lt`/`LtEql`/`Gt`/`GtEql` need `Order[T]`), boolean combinators (`And`/`Or`/`Not`, plus `True`/`False`), set membership (`In[T]` over a static `List[T]`), list membership (`Contains[T]`), null tests (`IsNull[T]` over `Term[Option[T]]`), and string matching (`Matches` regex, `StartsWith`). `Like` (case-(in)sensitive SQL-style `%`/`_` matching) lives in the sql-core module, not core.

keyConcepts.name: Filter / OrderBy / Offset / Limit / Count query nodes
keyConcepts.explanation: Filtering and paging are `Query` ADT nodes that wrap a `child` query: `Filter(pred, child)` keeps matching elements; `OrderBy(OrderSelections(sels), child)` sorts; `Offset(num, child)` drops the first num; `Limit(num, child)` truncates; `Count(child)` replaces a list with its element count. They compose by nesting.

keyConcepts.name: OrderSelection / OrderSelections
keyConcepts.explanation: `OrderSelection[T: Order](term, ascending = true, nullsLast = true)` describes one sort key over a `Term[T]`; multiple selections are combined in priority order inside `OrderSelections(List(...))`, which can sort an in-memory `Seq[Cursor]`. `ascending` controls direction; `nullsLast` controls null placement (SQL backends pass `nullsHigh` here).

keyConcepts.name: FilterOrderByOffsetLimit constructor/extractor
keyConcepts.explanation: `Query.FilterOrderByOffsetLimit` is the idiomatic way to build the whole stack from `Option`s: it nests `Filter` innermost, then `OrderBy`, then `Offset`, then `Limit` outermost. Its matching `unapply` lets interpreters destructure an arbitrary nesting back into `(pred, oss, offset, limit, child)`. Used heavily by the paging mappings.

keyConcepts.name: Elaboration via Elab.transformChild
keyConcepts.explanation: Filters/orders/limits are installed during compilation in a `SelectElaborator`. The elaborator matches `(ParentType, fieldName, List(Binding(...)))` and returns an `Elab[Unit]`, most commonly `Elab.transformChild(child => ...)` which rewrites the child query to add the desired nodes. `transformChild` is overloaded to accept `Query => Query`, `Query => Result[Query]`, or `Query => Elab[Query]`.

keyConcepts.name: Paging patterns (offset/limit, counted, has-more)
keyConcepts.explanation: Plain offset/limit just emits `Offset`/`Limit`. 'Counted' paging (SqlPaging1/2) exposes `offset`/`limit`/`total` by stashing paging info in the `Elab` environment, computing `items` via `FilterOrderByOffsetLimit` and `total` via `Count`. 'Has-more' paging (SqlPaging3) overfetches by one (`limit + 1`), uses `TransformCursor` + `ListTransformCursor` to trim the extra row, and reports `hasMore`. There is no Relay edges/cursor connection type in the repo; cursor-based paging is built by hand on these primitives.

  offset = offset,   // Option[Int]

CursorField("offset", CountryPaging.genOffset, Nil),
CursorField("limit",  CountryPaging.genLimit, Nil),
SqlField("total", root.numCountries),
SqlObject("items")

gotchas: Term covariance is intentionally avoided: the source comment on `trait Term[T]` says 'fun fact: making this covariant crashes Scala 3'. Do not try to make Term/Predicate covariant.

Eql/NEql/In/Contains require an implicit Eq[T]; Lt/LtEql/Gt/GtEql and OrderSelection require an implicit Order[T]. Forgetting the instance (or comparing the wrong static type) is a compile error. The element type must match the field's mapped type, including Option — e.g. OrderSelection[Option[String]] for a nullable string field, and IsNull[Int] over an Option[Int] field.

`Like` is NOT in the core predicate ADT — it lives in the sql-core module (grackle.sql.Like, with separate scala-2 and scala-3 source files) and is only meaningful against a SQL backend. Its first parameter is a union type `Term[String] | Term[Option[String]]` so it accepts both nullable and non-nullable string terms.

Path.asTerm silently picks ListPath vs UniquePath based on rootTpe.pathIsList(path). A scalar path used where a List term is expected (or vice versa) will compile via the path2Term/path2ListTerm implicits but fail at runtime: UniquePath.apply errors with 'Expected exactly one element for path ...' if the focus isn't a single ScalarFocus.

FilterOrderByOffsetLimit nests in a fixed order: Filter innermost, then OrderBy, then Offset, then Limit outermost. If you hand-nest the four Query nodes yourself in a different order, SQL compilation and the FilterOrderByOffsetLimit.unapply extractor may not recognize the pattern.

OrderSelection.nullsLast defaults to true, but SQL backends should pass `nullsLast = nullsHigh` (a per-dialect Boolean from SqlMapping) so null ordering matches the database; hardcoding true can produce results that differ between in-memory and SQL execution.

Argument validation lives in the elaborator, not the predicate. The example mappings reject offset < 0 and limit <= 0 with Result.failure inside mkOffset/mkLimit; an Offset(negative, ...) or Limit(0, ...) node is not validated by the Query ADT itself.

Counted/total paging needs a real backing count source. SqlPaging1 maps `total` to a column (root.numCountries) or compiles `Count(Select("items", Select(countAttr)))` to a SQL COUNT; you cannot get an accurate total just from the (possibly limited) items list.

'Has more' paging overfetches limit+1 rows ONLY when both `hasMore` and `items` are selected (it checks Elab.hasField). If you compute hasMore differently you must replicate this conditional, and you must use TransformCursor/ListTransformCursor to hide the extra row from clients — otherwise the extra item leaks into the response.

Predicate.and/or smart constructors and And.combineAll fold lists into chains and short-circuit on True/False; an empty list yields True (for and / combineAll) or False (for or). Building And/Or directly from an empty list of leaves is on you to guard.

There is no built-in Relay connection type (no edges/node/pageInfo/endCursor/hasNextPage) anywhere in this repo. 'Cursor-based' paging here means hand-rolled over Offset/Limit/Count/TransformCursor plus the GraphQL Cursor type — not the Relay spec. Documentation should not imply a ready-made Relay connection helper exists.

summary: Grackle models the outcome of every fallible operation (parsing, compilation, elaboration, query interpretation, validation, effects) as `Result[A]` — an `Ior`-like ADT with four cases: `Success` (value only), `Warning` (value + a non-empty chain of `Problem`s), `Failure` (problems only, no value), and `InternalError` (a `Throwable` representing a bug/unexpected condition, not a user-facing GraphQL error). `Problem` is the GraphQL-spec-shaped error object (message, locations, path, extensions) that gets serialised into the `errors` array of a response. The companion provides constructors and conversions, while `ResultInstances` supplies cats typeclass instances (`MonadError`, `Traverse`, `Parallel`, `Semigroup`, `Eq`) so results compose with `for`/`traverse`/`parMapN` and accumulate problems. At the response boundary `Mapping.mkResponse` folds a `Result[Json]` into a GraphQL response: `Success`→`{data}`, `Warning`→`{errors,data}`, `Failure`→`{errors}` (no data), and `InternalError`→raised into the effect `F`. `ValidationFailure` is a separate, schema/mapping-construction-time diagnostic type (with `Severity`) used for richly-formatted, colourised validation messages, distinct from runtime `Problem`s.

keyConcepts.name: Four-case Result ADT (Ior semantics)
keyConcepts.explanation: Result[+T] is sealed with Success(value), Warning(problems, value), Failure(problems) and InternalError(error). It generalises Either/Ior: Warning carries BOTH a value and accumulated problems (like Ior.Both), Failure carries only problems, and InternalError is a fourth case for Throwables that escape the normal problem channel. hasValue is true for Success/Warning; hasProblems is true for Warning/Failure; isInternalError isolates the bug case.

keyConcepts.name: Problem vs InternalError vs ValidationFailure
keyConcepts.explanation: Problem is a user-facing GraphQL error (serialised into the errors array). InternalError wraps a Throwable that should surface as an effect-level failure (M.raiseError in mkResponse), NOT as a GraphQL error — it represents an internal bug/unexpected state. ValidationFailure (with Severity Error/Warning/Info) is a third, unrelated diagnostic used only when building/validating a Schema or Mapping; ValidationException wraps a NonEmptyList of them.

keyConcepts.name: Problem accumulation via Semigroup/Applicative
keyConcepts.explanation: Problems accumulate as a NonEmptyChain[Problem]. flatMap and the MonadError carry warnings forward and merge problem chains; the Parallel/Applicative ap and the Semigroup combine accumulate problems from both sides (Failure ++ Failure = Failure with both, but a short-circuit on InternalError). This is how multiple validation/compilation errors are reported at once rather than failing on the first.

keyConcepts.name: Result combinators & syntax
keyConcepts.explanation: Instance methods: map, flatMap, traverse, fold, foldLeft/Right, toEither, toOption, withProblems, combine, getOrElse, plus predicates hasValue/isFailure/hasProblems/isInternalError/toProblems. Companion constructors: apply/pure/success, warning, failure, internalError, fromOption, fromEither, fromProblems, catchNonFatal, combineAllWithDefault. Extension syntax in grackle.syntax: a.success, opt.toResult(ifNone), opt.toResultOrError(ifNone).

keyConcepts.name: ResultT monad transformer
keyConcepts.explanation: ResultT[F[_], A](value: F[Result[A]]) lifts Result into an effect F (typically a cats-effect IO or fs2 Stream). It is used pervasively in the interpreter/mapping to thread Result through F with for-comprehensions; it preserves Warning/Failure/InternalError propagation and problem accumulation across the F boundary. Constructors: liftF, pure, fromResult, success, warning, failure, internalError.

keyConcepts.name: Mapping failures to the GraphQL response
keyConcepts.explanation: Mapping.mkResponse(result: Result[Json]): F[Json] is the single boundary that turns a Result into a spec response. Success→{"data":..}; Warning→{"errors":[..],"data":..} (errors AND data present); Failure→{"errors":[..]} (no data key); InternalError→M.raiseError(throwable). The overload mkResponse(data, errors) also emits a synthetic {"errors":[{"message":"Invalid query"}]} when both data and errors are empty.

keyConcepts.name: Severity ordering for validation
keyConcepts.explanation: ValidationFailure.Severity is a sealed trait (Error > Warning > Info) with a cats Order instance (Error=3, Warning=2, Info=1), letting validators filter/threshold diagnostics by severity (e.g. only fail on Error, surface Warning/Info).
