summary: This subsystem covers everything that turns a GraphQL query document into Grackle's internal query algebra apart from the data-fetching mapping itself: GraphQL introspection (`__schema`, `__type`, `__typename`), the built-in `@skip`/`@include` directives, custom query directives, named and inline fragment expansion (with type-condition narrowing), operation variables, and input-value coercion (both literal arguments and JSON variable values). Almost all of it is handled automatically by fixed compiler phases (`IntrospectionElaborator`, `VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator`, `MergeFields`) that run before the user's own elaborators; the only things a user configures are (1) whether introspection is `Full`/`TypenameOnly`/`Disabled` per query, (2) declaring custom directives in their SDL plus writing a `Phase` to interpret them, and (3) custom `SelectElaborator.select` logic which receives elaborated arguments and directives. Introspection is itself implemented as a separate self-contained `ValueMapping` over a fixed meta-schema (`Introspection.schema`) that is run on demand when an `Introspect` node is reached. Input coercion (custom-scalar widening, ID-from-String/Int, enum validation, defaulting, `@oneOf` enforcement, unknown-field rejection) is performed centrally in `Value.checkValue` / `Value.checkVarValue`.

keyConcepts.name: IntrospectionLevel (Full / TypenameOnly / Disabled)
keyConcepts.explanation: A per-query knob passed to compile / compileAndRun controlling which introspection meta-fields are allowed. Full enables __schema, __type and __typename; TypenameOnly allows only __typename (and rejects __schema/__type with 'Introspection is disabled'); Disabled removes the IntrospectionElaborator phase entirely so __schema/__type fall through to normal field resolution and fail with 'No field "__type" for type Query', while __typename is rejected with 'Introspection is disabled'. Defined in QueryCompiler.IntrospectionLevel.

keyConcepts.name: IntrospectionElaborator phase
keyConcepts.explanation: Compiler Phase (built automatically, prepended before the user's phases) that rewrites UntypedSelect nodes named __typename/__schema/__type into Introspect(schema, sel) nodes, subject to the IntrospectionLevel. IntrospectionElaborator(level) returns None when level is Disabled so the phase is omitted. It also re-roots fragment children against the introspection meta-schema so introspection fragments type-check.

keyConcepts.name: Introspect query node + Introspection.interpreter
keyConcepts.explanation: At runtime an Introspect(schema, query) node is executed by a dedicated interpreter Introspection.interpreter(targetSchema) which is a ValueMapping over the fixed meta-schema (Introspection.schema). The target schema's types/directives are exposed as plain Scala values (Type, Field, DirectiveDef, etc.) via ValueFields. __typename is special-cased and answered without invoking the full introspection mapping.

keyConcepts.name: VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator phase
keyConcepts.explanation: The single automatic phase that does four jobs in one pass: substitutes variable references into argument/directive values (Value.elaborateValue), evaluates @skip/@include and drops guarded subtrees (yielding Query.Empty), expands named fragment spreads and inline fragments into Group/Narrow nodes, and validates leaf vs structured subselection. It strips skip/include from the directive list before handing remaining directives to Directive.elaborateDirectives.

keyConcepts.name: @skip / @include semantics
keyConcepts.explanation: Built-in DirectiveDefs (DirectiveDef.Skip, DirectiveDef.Include) allowed on FIELD, FRAGMENT_SPREAD and INLINE_FRAGMENT. isSkipped computes (skip && if) || (include && !if). The 'if' argument may be a literal BooleanValue or a Boolean variable; a missing/non-Boolean argument or duplicate skip/include on one node fails compilation. Skipped nodes become Query.Empty and disappear from the result; the directives themselves never reach the data mapping.

keyConcepts.name: Fragment expansion and type narrowing
keyConcepts.explanation: Named fragments (...frag) and inline fragments (... on T / ...) are expanded at compile time. If the context type is already a subtype of the fragment's type condition the children are inlined directly; otherwise they are wrapped in a Narrow(ref, child). fragmentApplies implements the spec's 'fragment spread is possible' rule via schema.subtypes intersection. Fragment definition errors (undefined, unused, duplicate, cyclic, incompatible type condition) are detected before/at elaboration.

keyConcepts.name: Variables: definition, typing, coercion
keyConcepts.explanation: compileVarDefs turns $name: T var defs into InputValue defs against the target schema; compileVars coerces the supplied JSON variable values with Value.checkVarValue. Undefined and (optionally) unused variables are reported by validateVariablesAndFragments. Variable references inside arguments/lists/objects are only resolved during the VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator phase via Value.elaborateValue.

keyConcepts.name: Input value coercion (checkValue vs checkVarValue)
keyConcepts.explanation: Two parallel coercion routines resolve a value against an InputValue definition: checkValue for literal query values (Value -> Value) and checkVarValue for JSON variable values (Json -> Value). Both apply defaults for absent values, enforce nullability, validate enums (e.hasValue), widen Int/String to ID and primitives to custom scalars, recurse into lists and input objects, reject unknown object fields, and enforce @oneOf (exactly one non-null member).

keyConcepts.name: @oneOf input objects
keyConcepts.explanation: Input object types declared `input X @oneOf` are enforced during coercion: exactly one member field must be present and non-null. Violations (zero present, >1 present, present-but-null) produce specific errors. isOneOf is also surfaced via introspection on __Type.isOneOf, and the oneOf directive itself appears in __schema.directives.

keyConcepts.name: Custom query directives
keyConcepts.explanation: A custom directive is declared in SDL (e.g. `directive @upperCase on FIELD`) so it is registered in schema.directives and passes Directive.validateDirectivesForQuery location/argument checks. Behaviour is supplied by writing a QueryCompiler.Phase whose transform matches UntypedSelect nodes carrying that directive. Built-in skip/include/deprecated/specifiedBy/oneOf are always added (DirectiveDef.builtIns); user directives merge on top.

keyConcepts.name: Automatic vs configured
keyConcepts.explanation: Automatic: introspection elaboration & execution, __typename, @skip/@include, fragment expansion/validation, variable substitution & coercion, input coercion, @oneOf, deprecation filtering of introspection results, merge of duplicate fields. Configured by the user: introspectionLevel per query, custom directive SDL + interpreting Phase, custom SelectElaborator.select for field arguments, and whether unused vars/fragments are reported (reportUnused).

minimalExamples.title: Run an introspection query (__type) against a mapping
minimalExamples.explanation: Introspection is on by default (introspectionLevel = Full). No mapping for the __ meta-types is needed: Grackle rewrites __type into an Introspect node and runs the built-in Introspection meta-mapping over the target schema. Verbatim from IntrospectionSuite 'simple type query'.

minimalExamples.title: Disable introspection (and the TypenameOnly middle ground)
minimalExamples.explanation: introspectionLevel is the only thing you configure to gate introspection. Disabled drops the IntrospectionElaborator phase so __type falls through to normal field resolution; TypenameOnly keeps __typename but rejects schema/type introspection. From IntrospectionSuite 'introspection disabled' and 'introspection disabled typename allowed'.

minimalExamples.title: @skip / @include with Boolean variables
minimalExamples.explanation: @skip/@include are handled entirely automatically by VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator. Guarded subtrees that are skipped become Query.Empty and vanish from the compiled algebra; the directives never reach the data mapping. From SkipIncludeSuite 'skip/include field'. They also work on fragment spreads and inline fragments.

minimalExamples.title: Named fragment, inline fragment and type narrowing
minimalExamples.explanation: Fragment spreads and inline fragments are expanded at compile time. Because profiles is an interface (Profile), each fragment whose type-condition is a subtype is wrapped in Narrow(T, ...). A supertype fragment (... on Profile) inlines directly without a Narrow. __typename becomes an Introspect node. Adapted from FragmentSuite 'typed fragment query' / 'inline fragment query'.

minimalExamples.title: Variables: definition, JSON values, and coercion into input objects
minimalExamples.explanation: JSON variable values are coerced by checkVarValue against the schema: 123 becomes an IDValue, and input-object fields not supplied become AbsentValue (not NullValue). Supplying an unknown field ('quux') fails with "Unknown field(s) 'quux' in input object value of type Pattern in variable values". From VariablesSuite 'object variable query'.

minimalExamples.title: Input value coercion: null vs absent vs defaults
minimalExamples.explanation: Coercion fills defaults for omitted fields with a defaultValue, and yields AbsentValue for omitted nullable fields (vs NullValue for an explicit `null`). Top-level field(arg: null) => NullValue, field with no arg => AbsentValue. From InputValuesSuite 'input object value' and 'null value'.

minimalExamples.title: @oneOf input object enforcement
minimalExamples.explanation: Declaring an input object with @oneOf makes coercion enforce exactly one present, non-null member. Zero members, more than one, or a present-but-null member all fail with specific messages. Works for both literal args and variable values. From InputValuesSuite / VariablesSuite oneOf tests.

minimalExamples.title: Custom query directive: declare in SDL + interpret with a Phase
minimalExamples.explanation: A custom directive must be (1) declared in the SDL so it is registered in schema.directives and passes Directive.validateDirectivesForQuery (location/arg checks), and (2) interpreted by a user-written Phase prepended to compilerPhases. Note the directive is still on the UntypedSelect here because this phase runs before VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator strips non-skip/include directives. Verbatim from QueryDirectivesSuite.

gotchas: AbsentValue vs NullValue are distinct: an omitted argument/input-object field coerces to AbsentValue, an explicit `null` coerces to NullValue. Mappings and elaborators must handle both. Visible in InputValuesSuite 'null value' (field => AbsentValue, field(arg: null) => NullValue) and in every object-coercion test where omitted fields appear as AbsentValue.

Disabled vs TypenameOnly produce different errors for the same query. With Disabled, __type/__schema are not rewritten and fail later with "No field '__type' for type Query"; __typename fails with "Introspection is disabled". With TypenameOnly, __schema/__type fail with "Introspection is disabled" but __typename still resolves. (compiler.scala IntrospectionElaborator.transform; IntrospectionSuite).

Introspection field-resolution is reversed: when introspection is Disabled the IntrospectionElaborator phase is entirely absent (IntrospectionElaborator.apply returns None), so meta-fields are treated as ordinary schema fields. Don't assume a uniform 'introspection disabled' error message.

@skip and @include are stripped before custom directive elaboration. VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator filters out skip/include from the directive list before calling Directive.elaborateDirectives, and skipped nodes become Query.Empty. A custom Phase that inspects directives must run before this phase (prepend it to compilerPhases) or the directives may already be gone — but skip/include themselves are never visible to user phases that run after it.

Custom directives MUST be declared in the SDL. An undeclared directive triggers "Undefined directive 'x'" and a directive used at a wrong location triggers "Directive 'x' is not allowed on <LOCATION>" via Directive.validateDirectivesForQuery, run before the phases. Declaring `directive @upperCase on FIELD` only validates placement; it does NOT give behaviour — you still need an interpreting Phase.

Custom directive validation failures are warnings, not hard failures in the test example: the upperCase-on-Int case uses Elab.warning, so the query still returns data alongside an error entry. Whether a directive misuse aborts the query depends on whether your Phase yields Elab.failure or Elab.warning.

The skip/include 'if' argument must be Boolean (literal or Boolean variable). A non-Boolean variable, a missing 'if', or duplicate skip/include on one node fail with messages like "Argument of skip/include must be boolean", "Directive 'x' must have a single Boolean 'if' argument", or "skip/include directives must be unique" (VariablesSkipAndFragmentElaborator.isSkipped/extractCond).

Variables are validated for being defined AND unused. An undefined variable fails ("Variable 'x' is undefined"); an unused declared variable fails ("Variable 'x' is unused") unless you pass reportUnused = false. Same dual check applies to fragments ("Fragment 'x' is unused" / "is undefined"). See VariablesSuite and FragmentSuite.

Fragment validation is strict and happens up front: undefined fragment, duplicate fragment name, fragment cycles ("Fragment cycle starting from 'x'"), and type-incompatible spreads are all rejected. A supertype fragment that selects a subtype-only field fails ("No field 'name' for type Profile") — you must narrow with `... on User` inside the supertype fragment. (FragmentSuite supertype tests.)

Custom scalars are widened permissively during coercion: any of Int/Float/String/Boolean (and EnumValue-as-String) literals are accepted for a non-built-in ScalarType without validation (Value.checkValue/checkVarValue `if !s.isBuiltIn` branches). Grackle does not type-check custom scalar contents at this stage — that is the mapping's responsibility.

ID coercion is automatic and lossy-looking: StringValue and IntValue are coerced to IDValue (Int via i.toString). So a query literal `id: 123` and variable `123` both become IDValue("123"). Don't rely on receiving an IntValue for an ID-typed argument.

Unknown input-object fields are rejected but the error location string differs between paths: literal args say "... for input object value of type X in field 'f' of type 'Query'" (checkValue) while variable values say "... in input object value of type X in variable values" (checkVarValue). The wording is subtly different.

Introspection runs as a separate ValueMapping over Introspection.schema and is keyed by schema identity: SelectElaborator routes to elaborateIntrospection only when `s eq Introspection.schema`. The includeDeprecated args on fields/enumValues/inputFields/args default to false and are elaborated into Filter nodes (e.g. dropping deprecated fields) automatically — see SelectElaborator.elaborateIntrospection.

__typename is always permitted under Full and TypenameOnly and is special-cased in the interpreter (queryinterpreter.scala handles Introspect(_, Select("__typename", _, Empty))). It works inside named and inline fragments and supports aliasing (renamed: __typename). Only Disabled blocks it.

summary: This subsystem is the "serve a Mapping over HTTP" story. A `Mapping[F]` is a self-contained GraphQL endpoint: it exposes `compileAndRun` (single query/mutation -> one JSON response), `compileAndRunSubscription` (subscription -> fs2 `Stream[F, Json]` of responses), plus the lower-level `compiler`/`interpreter` that parse GraphQL text, bind variables, and produce a spec-shaped `{"data": ..., "errors": ...}` JSON envelope. These run-methods are transport-agnostic; Grackle ships no HTTP layer of its own. The canonical wiring lives in the `demo` module, which hand-rolls http4s routes (`GraphQLService.mkRoutes`) for GraphQL-over-HTTP GET and POST, an Ember server (`DemoServer.mkServer`), and an `IOApp` (`Main`). There is no built-in websocket / graphql-ws transport in the repo today; subscriptions are exposed only through the `Stream` API, and the demo server itself serves only GET/POST plus the static GraphQL Playground assets.

keyConcepts.name: Mapping as the runnable endpoint
keyConcepts.explanation: A `Mapping[F]` bundles a `Schema`, `typeMappings`, a lazily-built `compiler: QueryCompiler` and an `interpreter: QueryInterpreter[F]`. Everything you need to execute a query is on the mapping instance; `compileAndRun`/`compileAndRunSubscription` are the public entry points. You typically construct one mapping per GraphQL endpoint and route HTTP requests to it.

keyConcepts.name: compileAndRun vs compileAndRunSubscription
keyConcepts.explanation: `compileAndRunSubscription` is the primitive: it returns a `Stream[F, Json]` (one element per query/mutation, many elements for a subscription). `compileAndRun` is defined in terms of it: it runs the stream, asserts exactly one element, and `raiseError`s otherwise. So `compileAndRun` is for queries/mutations; subscriptions must use the streaming variant or they will fail at runtime with 'Result stream contained N results'.

keyConcepts.name: The GraphQL request triad: query / operationName / variables
keyConcepts.explanation: A GraphQL-over-HTTP request carries the query text (`text`/`query`), an optional `operationName` (`name`) used to pick one operation when the document defines several, and optional `variables` as a JSON object (`untypedVars: Option[Json]`). The demo extracts these from the URL query string (GET) or the JSON body (POST) and forwards them to `compileAndRun(query, op, vars)`.

keyConcepts.name: Compile then interpret pipeline
keyConcepts.explanation: `compileAndRunSubscription` calls `compiler.compile(text, name, untypedVars, introspectionLevel, reportUnused, env): Result[Operation]`, then `interpreter.run(op.query, op.rootTpe, env): Stream[F, Result[Json]]`, then `mkResponse` to turn each `Result[Json]` into the final envelope. Compilation does parsing, variable/fragment validation, field-merge validation, variable binding, directive validation, and the elaborator phases.

keyConcepts.name: The Operation type
keyConcepts.explanation: `Operation(query: Query, rootTpe: NamedType, directives: List[Directive])` is the compiled, executable form returned by the compiler: an elaborated query-algebra `Query`, the resolved root operation type (Query/Mutation/Subscription type from the schema), and any operation-level directives. `UntypedOperation` (with `UntypedQuery`/`UntypedMutation`/`UntypedSubscription` cases) is the pre-compilation parser output.

keyConcepts.name: GraphQL response envelope (mkResponse)
keyConcepts.explanation: `mkResponse` builds the spec response JSON: `{"data": ...}` on success, `{"errors": [...]}` (and optionally `data`) on failure, and `{"errors":[{"message":"Invalid query"}]}` when there is neither data nor errors. Crucially, a `Result.InternalError` is NOT turned into JSON: `mkResponse(result: Result[Json])` calls `M.raiseError`, so internal errors propagate as effect failures (HTTP 500 via http4s error handling), while GraphQL validation errors come back as a normal 200 with an `errors` array.

keyConcepts.name: IntrospectionLevel
keyConcepts.explanation: `compileAndRun`/compile take `introspectionLevel: IntrospectionLevel = Full`. `IntrospectionLevel` (in `compiler.scala`) has `Full`, `TypenameOnly`, and `Disabled`. `Full` lets clients run the standard `IntrospectionQuery` (needed by Playground/GraphiQL); `Disabled` rejects `__schema`/`__type` introspection; `TypenameOnly` allows only `__typename`.

keyConcepts.name: Env threading
keyConcepts.explanation: All run/compile methods accept `env: Env = Env.empty`. This is request-scoped context (e.g. auth/tenant info) made available to elaborators and effectful root fields. The demo does not use it, but tests show `compileAndRun(query, env = Env("secure" -> true))` reaching a `CursorField`/effect handler via `env.get`.

keyConcepts.name: http4s wiring (demo)
keyConcepts.explanation: `GraphQLService.mkRoutes[F: Concurrent](prefix)(mapping)` builds `HttpRoutes[F]` with a GET case (query/operationName/variables from the query string, variables decoded via a custom `QueryParamDecoder[Json]`) and a POST case (decode body `as[Json]`, pull `query`/`operationName`/`variables` fields). `DemoServer.mkServer` wraps routes with a static-asset route (Playground), `Logger`, `ErrorHandling`, and an `EmberServerBuilder` on 0.0.0.0:8080. `Main` constructs each mapping as a `Resource`, maps it through `mkRoutes`, combines routes with `<+>`, and `useForever`s the server.

gotchas: compileAndRun on a subscription fails at runtime, not compile time: it collects the result stream and raises IllegalStateException 'Result stream contained N results; expected exactly one.' (or 'Result stream was empty.'). Use compileAndRunSubscription for subscriptions.

Grackle ships NO HTTP or websocket transport. The entire http4s/Ember wiring lives in the demo module and is example code you copy, not a published API. There is no graphql-ws / graphql-transport-ws implementation anywhere in the repo; subscriptions are only reachable via the Stream returned by compileAndRunSubscription. Wiring that to a websocket is left to you.

Internal errors do not become GraphQL error JSON. mkResponse(result) calls M.raiseError on Result.InternalError, so it surfaces as an effect failure -> HTTP 500 (the demo catches it with ErrorHandling.Recover.total + Logger). Only GraphQL validation/execution failures (Result failures) are returned as a normal 200 response with an "errors" array.

Multi-operation documents require operationName. If the document defines more than one operation you MUST pass name; otherwise compile fails with 'Operation name required to select unique operation'. With a single operation, name may be None. Also 'Query shorthand cannot be combined with multiple operations' and 'No operation named ...'/'Multiple operations named ...' are possible failures.

variables must be a JSON object (Option[Json]). compileVars fails with 'Variables must be represented as a Json object' if you pass a non-object Json. In the demo's GET route, variables arrive as a URL-encoded JSON string and are parsed by a custom QueryParamDecoder[Json]; a malformed value yields a 400 BadRequest ('Invalid variables'), separate from GraphQL validation.
reportUnused defaults to true: unused variables/fragments are reported (as warnings/errors accumulated in the Result). Set reportUnused = false to silence that during variable/fragment validation.

Schema validation is deferred to first use. The compiler is a lazy val and calling it runs typeMappings.unsafeValidateIfChecked(); a mis-specified mapping won't blow up until the first request is compiled (unless you force the compiler earlier).

IntrospectionLevel defaults to Full. GraphQL client tools (Playground/GraphiQL) issue an IntrospectionQuery; setting Disabled (or TypenameOnly) will break their schema discovery while still allowing normal queries.

The demo's POST handler only reads top-level fields query/operationName/variables and requires query to be present (InvalidMessageBodyFailure 'Missing query field'); it does not implement batched operations or persisted queries.

Routes are combined with the SemigroupK <+> (from cats) on HttpRoutes, and DemoServer wraps everything in orNotFound, Logger, and a *total* ErrorHandling.Recover so uncaught throwables are logged rather than crashing the server.
